bank.retain_mission: Evidence policy 2. Write extracted facts in English for the English embedding model, while preserving names, code, and literal values. This is one global memory bank across the user's coding-agent sessions. Extract the fewest durable facts: explicit user preferences, corrections, constraints, final technical decisions, environment facts, successful methods, useful failure causes, and completed outcomes. Preserve exact identifiers and values. Keep the named task, project, machine, and conditions; do not turn a scoped setting into a global preference. A user statement is not the same as an assistant report. Attribute unverified assistant claims as reports, not independently verified facts. Explicit user corrections have the highest authority. Assistant text marked memory-assisted is derived context and must not create independent evidence. Ignore generated memory, harness instructions, injected context, greetings, connectivity-test chatter without a technical outcome, transient status reports, and progress chatter. A compact action records an attempted action, not proof of its result. Follow source-entry timestamps and parent links; different branches are alternatives, not a single sequence of decisions. Record the latest supported state with the earlier state explicitly marked superseded when useful. Preserve the time zone of an explicit timestamp. Never label an unqualified prose time as UTC or invent an exact date. Distinguish when a statement was recorded from when its described event occurred. If the source does not support a fact, do not extract it.
bank.observations_mission: Write evidence-backed observations in English for future coding sessions, preserving names, code, and literal values. Distinguish user statements, assistant reports, and verified outcomes. Do not promote suggestions, generated memory, memory-assisted prose, or attempted actions to independent proof. Explicit user corrections take priority. Preserve the latest supported state and label superseded states as historical; do not reverse a correction merely because an older report is repeated. If sources conflict without a supported resolution, state the conflict instead of choosing a winner. Preserve exact values, task and machine scope, and source time zones. Do not merge settings for different tasks or machines into one conflicting fact. Do not invent UTC offsets or treat a report's timestamp as its event date. Prefer one concise observation per topic over summaries that combine unrelated operational states.
